lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Derik, I heard you live in...Yuen Long?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes I do. You live in Kowloon, don’t you?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Hmm, yes, I’ve been living in Kowloon whole my life, so I don’t really have an idea how Yuen Long is like. Even though I’m a Hongkonger.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes. So Yuen Long is well...pretty typical Hong Kong. Uh...those people in Yuen Long are supposed to be...indigenous, you know, a lot of them are. Of course I’m myself not indigenous, since I’ve been living in Yuen Long for...around two years. Before that I lived in Shatin. Yep.
So uh Yuen Long is quite a unique place. Because...in the beginning I had...a lot of fantasies about this place, like ‘will there be cows?’ and so on, like very rural areas.
So when I arrived there (by public transport), it was a realisation - whoa! I thought I was in Nathan Road. You live in Kowloon, don’t you?

You know how Nathan Road is like: very prosperous...it’s one huge road, while the two sides are...uh old buildings, new buildings, all mixed together. So Yuen Long has that too. It has a large road, which is...one...but the large road in Yuen Long, while resembling Nathan Road, is only one section of that.

It...after one segment, out there, on the two sides, it’s all green, yep. Yes, you’re already in the mountains. But that one section itself is very prosperous. Yuen Long residents call that place ‘the big road’. As far as I remember, it’s actually the Yuen Long section of Castle Peak Road.

So uh, Yuen Long itself, it’s...a place that the Kowloon people among us sometimes find very out of the way and inconvenient. But this place, once you live there, you’ll realise that it might even be more convenient than Kowloon – you never know! Why?

Because Yuen Long, the Yuen Long town centre, uh it’s all concentrated in one area. On the Yuen Long ‘Big Road’ and Kau Yuk Road – two big roads, there. Just that area! So, all...the stores selling stuff, tasty stuff...restaurants, cinemas, everything is packed right there.

Yup so supposing you live in Mong Kok, when you want to buy stuff at Fortress and want to compare the prices with...Broadway, you might end up walking several blocks. Whereas in Yuen Long, you simply walk along those two roads and see everything.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: When you talk about it, it sounds kind of like um...the downtowns you see abroad.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yup that’s right.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: As in...the residents would uh...not go out and find...everywhere...em I mean, stores and so on. Even in Yuen Long...I mean like...is it convenient to get out there from home? When you want to buy these things? Like daily (supplies)?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: OK gaa3! It’s pretty easy!

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: It’s...convenient enough?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: It depends...depends where exactly you live. Of course, if you live in the areas around the walled villages, uh you might have to take...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Yes! In my head I keep having the image of the walled villages in my head. Whenever you talk about Yuen Long, I’m thinking about those.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: They are there!

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: So while...while you were talking to me about these things, I couldn’t picture them at all, because all that was in my head was walled villages, Poon Choi, and lots of elderly people...

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yes!

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I mean...it doesn’t feel like there’d be any young people living there.

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Yuen Long...has the...the walled villages you’re picturing. Yep, on the outskirts of Yuen Long town centre. Most of the time, uh...you can get to many villages in 20 minutes...by minibus. You can get to the town centre. But speaking of young people, uh, there are indeed popular places for them too, especially like...B-zai (Kei Kee) Dessert, which is something you’ve definitely heard of, if we’re talking about Yuen Long. Yes, every Saturday, you can see tons of gorgeous sports cars parked there...

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Whoa...

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: So it’s very...there’s the densest group of young girls I’ve ever seen in my life. Yep, when you eat sweet soup there, you can forget about staring at the sweet soup – everyone there gawks [at the girls]. Yeah looking around, yeah lots of things to see. Yep it’s a pretty funny/intriguing place. You can come for a walk if you’re interested.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: I can? Can I come visit you too?

lines.speaker: Derik
lines.english: Of course! Yes but I don’t live there anymore now. I can go there together with you though!

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.english: Oh! Great. Not bad.
